xtmux-r6g.8.description:
Finish the release deliverable from xtmux-r6g.1: publish @jaggerxtrm/xtmux to npm. Deferred out of sprint because it needs one-time npmjs.com configuration (not a repo change).

## Context

- v0.1.0 tagged and GH-released 2026-07-17: https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtmux/releases/tag/v0.1.0
- release.yml (main) already contains `npm publish --access public --provenance`; the last run failed with `404 The requested resource '@jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.1.0' could not be found or you do not have permission to access it.` The package has never actually been published — curl on the registry returns `{"error":"Not found"}`; PR#20 shipped the tarball infra but no tag ever fired the workflow before.
- Failed run for reference: https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtmux/actions/runs/29545471622

## Two paths (pick one)

### Path A — OIDC Trusted Publisher (matches current workflow, keeps provenance)

1. On npmjs.com, log in as the `@jaggerxtrm` scope owner.
2. Navigate to the org/scope settings → Trusted Publishers.
3. Add a publisher: repo `Jaggerxtrm/xtmux`, workflow file `.github/workflows/release.yml`, environment blank.
4. Re-run https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtmux/actions/runs/29545471622 (or move v0.1.0 tag to head to trigger a fresh run).

No repo changes required.

### Path B — Classic token (fastest, drops provenance for now)

1. `npm token create --type automation` (or the modern granular equivalent) on the `@jaggerxtrm` scope.
2. Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret: `NPM_TOKEN`.
3. In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, replace the publish step:
   ```yaml
   - env: { NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }} }
     run: npm publish --access public
   ```
4. Re-run the failed release (as above).

Path A is preferred long-term because provenance stays.

## Acceptance

- `npm view @jaggerxtrm/xtmux versions` returns `[ '0.1.0' ]`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes cleanly on the NEXT tag push without manual intervention.
- Bead xtmux-r6g.1 already documents the release cadence; no doc changes needed here unless Path B is chosen (add a comment on why provenance was skipped).

source.description:
Post-3ua polish sprint: help surfaces, npm/GitHub release hygiene, xtmux monitor UX, sp console TUI aggregation, /planning library-first pipeline, memory-processor overhaul.

## Motivation

The two recent epics (xtmux-j46 runtime contracts + xtmux-3ua SQLite reply/wake SSOT, 42 merged PRs on xtmux; parallel work on core+specialists) shipped fast. User-facing surfaces have drifted:
- Help output, README, skill docs may not represent everything that landed
- npm packages ship internal docs (plans/design under docs/) that don't belong in distribution
- No `repository`/`homepage`/`bugs` fields on `xtrm-cli` and `@jaggerxtrm/specialists`
- xtmux has zero GitHub releases despite v0.10-era features
- git-cliff config in core+specialists inlines full commit bodies — noisy CHANGELOG
- xtmux monitor/logging surfaces got great JSON but the human-view is missing
- sp console TUI is slow on aggregated view; opportunity to unify with xtmux pane/monitor state
- /planning skill lets agents invent instead of surfacing existing deps first
- memory-processor skill+specialist is broken: 500+ memories → runs fail, when they pass ~50 memories are forgotten. It doesn't anchor cleaning to landed PRs/releases

## Workstreams (child beads)

W1 xtmux (Claude Opus, worker in xt claude worktree)
W2 core (pi codex-sol, worker in xt pi worktree)
W3 specialists+sp-TUI (pi codex-sol, worker in xt pi worktree)
W4 /planning skill library-first pipeline (Claude Opus, design-only worker)
W5 memory-processor overhaul (pi codex-sol, design + patch)

## Cross-cutting rules

- Cardinal multiplexing rules apply (never multi-line send-keys, never $() in send-keys, use safe-send-pointer, never send to working pane)
- Every worker's first action is `bd show <epic>` AND `bd show <own child>` — written verbatim into /tmp prompt file
- Each worker owns exactly one repo path; do not push outside SCOPE
- Model budget: Claude Opus for W1+W4 (design-heavy), pi codex/gpt-5.6-sol for W2/W3/W5 (implementation)
- RAM: 2.3Gi free at start, 12 cores, load avg 7-12. Stagger workers. Kill on completion.
- No new npm deps for W2/W3 unless already in package.json
- Ponytail: shortest working diff, no speculative abstractions

## Done when

All child beads closed with clean handoff notes. New GH releases visible for all three repos. Aggregated monitor/TUI proposal reviewed by user. Memory-processor and planning-skill diffs ready to apply.
source.notes:
## Addendum: automation + release semver rules (added by orchestrator mid-turn per user)

- After the manual regeneration and cleanup, WIRE `git-cliff` so subsequent regenerations are automated at the right step. Prefer whichever fits: a `release` GitHub Action, a pre-tag git hook, or an `xt end`/release script step. Pick one; document it in the repo.
- Cut a **npm publish** (for repos with a package.json) AND a **GitHub release** at the end.
- Version bumps: **minors and patches only** — no majors this sprint. Choose minor when this batch adds user-facing features (both epics land features), patch for pure fix/cleanup batches.
- xtmux (no npm) — GitHub release only.
